claims.claim: MobileBERT uses a thin deep architecture with bottleneck structures and a specially inverted-bottleneck BERT-large teacher.
claims.verification_note: Teacher is specialized; not an arbitrary vanilla BERT-large checkpoint.

claims.claim: MobileBERT reference paper claims 4.3x smaller and 5.5x faster than BERT-base in specified evaluations.
The paper reports 62 ms Pixel 4 latency under paper evaluation and GLUE score 77.7.
claims.verification_note: Not guaranteed for arbitrary Chinese tasks or mobile hardware.

claims.claim: ONNX Runtime defines dynamic quantization with runtime activation scale and static quantization with calibration data.
claims.verification_note: The quantization method must be coupled to supported ops and CPU.

claims.claim: Quantization can reduce task quality; ONNX Runtime documents debugging via FP32/quantized weight and activation matching.
claims.verification_note: Do not assume quantization is lossless or universally faster.

claims.claim: MobileBERT is task agnostic and supports downstream fine-tuning.
claims.verification_note: Task and tokenizer must be chosen per checkpoint.
